transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (CloudMart PM), Marco Silva (Cloud Architect), Priya Desai (Security)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — appreciate you making time. This is Lena from Redwood, AE on the partnership side. We also have Daniel, our SE.
[00:07] Daniel Cho: Hey all. I'll be covering the technical bits, perf, and reference arch.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: Hi! Aisha here — I'm CloudMart partner PM. We also have Marco and Priya. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Marco Silva: Morning/afternoon folks. Marco, cloud arch on CloudMart.
[00:22] Priya Desai: Priya — security lead. I'll mostly ask the compliance and KMS questions.
[00:27] Lena Park: Cool. Agenda, quick: one) marketplace listing requirements and what CloudMart needs from us, two) reference architecture options — public SaaS listing vs private VPC integration, three) security/compliance checklist, four) perf testing plan and known constraints, five) next steps. Does that look right?
[00:40] Aisha Rahman: Yep, that's what we had in mind. Also to discuss co-marketing assets and timelines.
[00:45] Lena Park: Great. I'll jump into the marketplace checklist first — we got the doc Aisha sent, thanks. The core asks from CloudMart are: listing metadata, deployment model options, manifest of APIs, SSO/KMS notes, and a reference arch that we can surface in the marketplace listing page.
[01:02] Aisha Rahman: Yeah, we need a short reference arch that maps to the CloudMart network model — whether vendors support private peering, or whether they use a SaaS-on-cloudmart pattern.
[01:10] Daniel Cho: Right, and from Redwood side we have two typical patterns: 1) Hosted Redwood API — standard SaaS listing where traffic goes to our hosted inference and we expose an integration webhook or API, 2) Dedicated/Private model — where we either provide a dedicated pool in our infra or we deploy a private instance into customer VPC / on-prem. We can show both in the ref arch.
[01:29] Marco Silva: For CloudMart we prefer the marketplace to support a private integration option — many enterprise customers want the VPC flow or at least private connectivity. How do you handle KMS and key separation in that mode?
[01:38] Daniel Cho: Good question. In private deploys we support customer-managed KMS keys — we have integrations with common KMS providers. For the managed Dedicated option we can also support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via an HSM-backed KMS. I'll attach specific docs. (slight cough) Note: sometimes our transcription or docs list K-V cache as KV cache, sorry if earlier notes were messy.
[01:58] Priya Desai: On that KMS point — do you rotate keys automatically? Where are audit logs stored? We need a clear SOC2 mapping.
[02:06] Lena Park: We do have SOC2. We keep audit logs in the control plane with configurable retention. For private deployments, logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM. Key rotation can be automated or customer-controlled depending on KMS provider. We'll send the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide.
[02:22] Priya Desai: Okay please send that. Also SSO — we need SAML metadata if you're integrating admin consoles for marketplace listing admin.
[02:29] Lena Park: Yup, we'll include SAML/SSO details.
[02:33] Aisha Rahman: For the marketplace listing template, we require the deployment options labeled clearly — e.g., SaaS (hosted), Dedicated (reserved capacity), Private (VPC/on-prem). Also pricing bands.
[02:44] Daniel Cho: We can provide pricing ranges and a per-token cost model for hosted with examples, and reserved pricing guidance for Dedicated. We'll indicate latencies for each model — hosted typical p95 latency Xms, dedicated lower variance. Note: numbers in the doc are indicative until we run a joint benchmark.
[02:59] Marco Silva: About benchmarks — we'd like an initial perf test in our staging that mimics typical CloudMart workload. Can you describe what you need?
[03:06] Daniel Cho: We'll want a staging account with an endpoint or network path. Ideally, we test both routes: 1) via public SaaS endpoints from CloudMart staging to Redwood hosted, and 2) via a private peering / VPC path to a Redwood Dedicated or private deploy. For the test we usually run a 10k qps synthetic with average request sizes — maybe 256–512 tokens — to observe batching behavior, throughput, and latency percentiles. We'll bring a BQM / script and share the raw results.
[03:31] Marco Silva: 10k qps is aggressive; for initial smoke maybe start smaller — 1k then scale — but we can schedule high-run later. We need the runbook.
[03:41] Daniel Cho: Sure, we'll start with 1k and ramp. I'll put details in the runbook.
[03:45] Lena Park: Quick question on billing and marketplace procurement — Aisha, does CloudMart manage marketplace billing and you need metering events?
[03:52] Aisha Rahman: Yes, we'll surface usage-based billing via our marketplace. We need events and record of tokens/usage; ideally a billing export and invoice reconciliation method.
[04:01] Lena Park: Redwood can emit usage metrics and billing exports; we can also integrate with your metering API. We'll include the metering schema.
[04:07] Priya Desai: On the data residency front — some customers will require that inference occurs in certain regions. Does Redwood support region pinning for hosted?
[04:14] Daniel Cho: We support region pinning and have multiple cloud regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. We'll detail region options in the ref arch.
[04:23] Aisha Rahman: Good. On legal/compliance side, we'll need a minimal set of EULA terms for the marketplace listing. I'll loop in legal after we have the technical artifacts.
[04:32] Lena Park: Sounds good. Next, reference architecture variants — Daniel, do you want to walk through the diagram?
[04:38] Daniel Cho: Yep. (paper rustle) High level: Option A: SaaS listing — CloudMart routes calls to our hosted API over TLS, typical OAuth or API key auth, standard web hooks for event notifications. Option B: Dedicated — reserved capacity where CowdMart customers get isolated GPU pools; integration via private peering and mutual TLS. Option C: Private deploy — Redwood control plane in Redwood cloud but compute in customer VPC or on-prem; this supports KMS BYOK and direct storage of logs in customer infra.
[05:01] Marco Silva: For option C, network wise — do you require direct cross-account roles, or do you deploy a VM/container into our VPC? How does the upgrade lifecycle look?
[05:10] Daniel Cho: We have a few models. We can deploy a managed runtime as containers into a customer's VPC (managed private) with our orchestration, or we can provide an appliance image for on-prem. Upgrades are handled via our orchestration with maintenance windows; customers can choose automatic or manual updates. We'll include a lifecycle table in the doc.
[05:27] Marco Silva: Ok that's helpful.
[05:29] Priya Desai: Who holds the PII in these models? If logs contain prompt data, we need an explicit data flow diagram so we can validate retention policies.
[05:37] Daniel Cho: Good point. In hosted mode Redwood may process prompts transiently and retain minimal logs per tenant with configurable retention; in private mode, logs can be kept in your storage and we can disable retention on our side. We'll provide the data flow and masking guidance.
[05:51] Aisha Rahman: On marketplace page we usually want a short diagram and a downloadable PDF reference arch. Can Redwood provide both?
[05:57] Lena Park: Yes — we'll prepare a short diagram and a PDF. We'll also include a sample marketplace listing blurbs.
[06:03] Marco Silva: Regarding the integrational APIs — your catalog mentions embeddings, text generation, and reranking. Are there any extra endpoints or batches we should be aware of for the marketplace?
[06:12] Daniel Cho: The main ones: completion/generation, chat API, embeddings, and a reranking API. Each has throughput and latency characteristics. For embeddings we have a batching-friendly flow; for chat we support streaming and function calls. We'll include API contract snippets in the marketplace manifest.
[06:27] Priya Desai: For streaming, does CloudMart support long-lived connections from browser clients? We might prefer server-to-server to avoid exposing creds.
[06:34] Lena Park: Agreed — best practice is server-to-server with token exchange. We can provide short-lived tokens for end-user flows.
[06:40] Aisha Rahman: Let's talk timelines. We want the listing live by end of Q2 — so target June. That means integration artifacts by March, perf validation April, legal/terms in May, and listing launch prep in June. Is that feasible?
[06:54] Daniel Cho: It's tight but doable. If we get the staging access this week and run the first perf runs by mid-March, that gives us time to iterate.
[07:02] Marco Silva: We can provision staging endpoints — Aisha will share onboarding steps.
[07:06] Aisha Rahman: I'll share the marketplace staging instructions and template after this call.
[07:11] Lena Park: Great. Now a few product-specific notes — our runtime supports prefix/KV caching which helps costs for repeat prompts; we'll call that out as a benefit when integrated via private peering too. Sometimes docs write it as "K-V cache" or "KV cache" so it'll be clear.
[07:26] Daniel Cho: Also quantization options and model variants — for Dedicated you can pin a quantized model which reduces GPU memory and cost while keeping latency within SLOs. We'll put recommended profiles per workload.
[07:37] Priya Desai: For the security checklist we need: SOC2 copy, network diagram, KMS and key rotation docs, SAML metadata, RBAC model, and audit log export format. Anything else?
[07:48] Lena Park: That covers most. Add data deletion policy and sample SLAs for Dedicated/Private.
[07:54] Priya Desai: Yes, add deletion policy.
[07:57] Aisha Rahman: On the co-marketing side — CloudMart will want a short case study template and logo assets. We'll align once the technical integration is proven.
[08:05] Lena Park: Happy to align on that.
[08:08] (brief pause, background noise)
[08:15] Daniel Cho: Quick note on metrics: for the perf tests please capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second, GPU utilization, and batching efficiency. We'll run with synthetic and a small real-world prompt corpus.
[08:29] Marco Silva: We'll make sure staging can capture network metrics and provide links to our telemetry.
[08:34] Aisha Rahman: On metering, we need usage granularity — per-token or per-request? Most listings are per usage unit (tokens) with tiered bands.
[08:43] Lena Park: Per-token is our primary billing unit for hosted; we can also provide per-inference billing for dedicated contracts. We'll include examples in the marketplace pricing table.
[08:53] Priya Desai: Any compliance red flags for the marketplace? We need to ensure the contract states responsibilities for data processing and controls.
[09:00] Lena Park: We'll provide an annotation of responsibilities. Redwood's standard DPA and security addendum covers data processing — we'll share that.
[09:07] Aisha Rahman: Great. Shall we go through the concrete deliverables and owners?
[09:12] Lena Park: Yes — 1) Redwood reference arch + PDF and short diagram — owner: Lena, due 2026-03-10. 2) Staging perf runs + runbook — owner: Daniel, initial results due 2026-03-18. 3) Security docs (SOC2 summary, KMS guide, SAML metadata) — owner: Priya to provide CloudMart specifics; Redwood to send ours; Redwood part due 2026-03-09. 4) Marketplace listing draft & pricing table — owner: Aisha with Redwood inputs; draft due 2026-03-11.
[09:40] Aisha Rahman: I'll circulate the marketplace template after this call.
[09:44] Marco Silva: For the perf test, one more ask — can Redwood provide a small test harness container we can run in staging to generate traffic?
[09:51] Daniel Cho: Yep, we'll share a dockerized load generator and the scenario scripts.
[09:56] Aisha Rahman: Perfect.
[10:00] (some overlap, unclear speaker) Speaker 3: ok yes, logs..
[10:04] Lena Park: Any other questions from CloudMart?
[10:07] Priya Desai: One last security question — does Redwood support submitting audit logs to our SIEM via syslog or S3?
[10:13] Daniel Cho: We support S3 forwarding and syslog via a collector. We'll provide the endpoints and a sample config.
[10:20] Aisha Rahman: OK that's all from me.
[10:23] Lena Park: Great. Quick recap — we'll share the ref arch, run perf tests, exchange security docs, and plan a marketing call late March. I'll email the links and attach the reference doc and runbook.
[10:36] Marco Silva: Thanks everyone.
[10:38] Daniel Cho: Thanks — I'll follow up with the runbook and perf scripts.
[10:42] Priya Desai: Thanks.
[10:43] Lena Park: Thanks all — talk soon.
